context: After many days of selling, 11 Sep produced a sudden RECOVERY -- and he flags it may be a REVERSAL, not a bounce. Then a two-three day holiday. So neither side is seated going in.
plan: EVERY OPEN SHAPE BUYS, but as a FOLLOW this time and not a hunt: 'such a market can be followed continuously', 'we can walk with the market'. Gap up, flat AND gap down all keep the same plan.

NEITHER SIDE IS SEATED, AND HE CHECKS BOTH: 'if in gap-up or flat we try to find any SELLER's SLs, we won't get them' -- and in the same breath, 'the BUYERS' SLs aren't here either'. There is nobody to squeeze in either direction.

THE HOLIDAY IS WHY THERE ARE NO BUYERS: the move was sudden AND a two-three day break followed, so 'not many people are sitting long here' and traders 'couldn't apply their minds'. Without the break this recovery would have recruited longs.

A GOOD GAP UP IS THE BEST CASE -- 'if a good gap up opens, that is best for us'. A gap down keeps the SAME buy plan 'because overall positive momentum has happened', so a red open is not a reason to flip.

HE FLAGS THE RECOVERY MAY BE A REVERSAL: 'any recovery can also be a reversal', so treat it as a possible turn in the multi-day downtrend. In FLAT he warns that 'sometimes there are some rejections in such a market'.
